rows.what the ink shows: An accented à, the initial m humps and paired tall t strokes of mettre remain visible in black. The continuation is crossed by the separate red Ajout annotation and its strokes; the surviving low curves and terminal upright do not distinguish net, point or après.

Sur has a small initial turn, shallow u and terminal hook; les has its high l and joined low ending. The last word has two p-like descending strokes and a later upright, but its compressed intervening letters, acute accent and final plural ending are not separately secure.

The initial tall stem and following i/l/b-like uprights are visible; the latter half runs into a thin horizontal trace and an indistinct terminal loop. Those ending strokes do not securely separate the short Hilbert form from the additional letters of hilbertiens.

A looped d is followed by an acute mark over é, the shallow v/e sequence, a tall l, then the low o and descending p group. The joined final er extends to the right beneath the diagonal cancellation crossing.

The large open C is clear, but much of the following sequence is flattened by thick horizontal ink; the q-like descent meets the underline. The small terminal group before the comma cannot establish an additional plural s, and the acute mark is not independently distinct.

A dense initial ch-like cluster and a long barred word precede a short low cluster and a final group with tall t-like strokes. Cancellation and underlining merge the interiors, so changement, de and notation cannot each be verified as complete words.

Several low separated strokes lead into a long horizontal run and a dark t-like upright near its end. The o/a loops and the final i-o-n-s sequence are not separately distinguishable in this compressed word.

The word between u and suivant contains a short initial curved group, a long dipping upright and a later hooked tall stroke, followed by an elevated dot and low tail. These features do not securely establish the opening letters or the accents required to select répétées, ordonnées or comptées.
The small deleted group is a dense low bowl with an upright left edge and a triangular overstroke. Its possible d ascender and e loop are merged with the cancellation, so de remains unconfirmed.

rows.what the ink shows: After que, the first group is a compact tall curved sign; the following low word is crossed diagonally, then a short double curve precedes a longer group with d/l-like rises. I cannot separately verify the article, suite, en and every letter of module, or distinguish la from leur.

The first group has crowded upright strokes and a long low exit; the second has a tall initial stroke, a detached dot and a descending terminal hook. The t/e sequence in cette and s/t/e sequence in liste remain too compressed to confirm both whole words.

The group before the line-ending qu'un has a low curved beginning and an upright obscured by the heavy diagonal slash. The internal n-t-i-e-n sequence and terminal t cannot be counted separately through that stroke.

Above and below the continuous deletion bar survive a loop, short uprights, dots and long low joins. The five proposed words d'une, infinité, de, valeurs and nulles, including the apostrophe and acute accent, cannot each be verified; the existing deleted layer is retained.

The crowded struck band preserves small upright and lowered strokes, while short horizontals merge with its long cancellation line. I cannot independently confirm lambda, its index i, both parentheses around u, the equality and zero, the words pour/les/autres, or the final i; the whole proposed sequence remains uncertain.

At the end of the crossed line before the next formula, low clusters with a dot, a rising stroke and a hooked end survive among the cancellation curves. They do not support a reliable lexical reading or an independently verified two-word count; the original count is preserved.

The leading rho group and equals are followed by an opening curve, lambda with a lowered i, then a tall opening curve and a dark doubled trough before the raised star; one further u is visible after the star. A closing curve, elevated 1/2 and two final closing curves are visible, but the initial u count and exact allocation of all parentheses remain unresolved; the narrower same-line u-star-u example does not settle the fused trough.

The word shows a long first p descent, a small rounded middle group and a second, shorter p-like downward stroke. The following r/e/s run ends in a long low rightward stroke, matching the same-page shape of propres without an added upright.
An initial curved upright and scattered lower hooks remain beneath two thick cancellation strokes. Neither the individual words nor the accent and apostrophe can be verified through those strokes.

A curved initial stroke and several small bowls survive along the horizontal cancellation. They do not separately establish Si, the isolated u, est, and unitaire; the candidate remains wholly uncertain.
The canceled tail before On obtient has a low black join and short uprights, without a secure internal word break. The inherited count of two words is not verified.

After On obtient, the first compact group meets a diagonal cancellation; two further groups contain low joins and a taller crossed stroke. These do not independently establish all three proposed words.
The word begins with a tall upright and foot, followed by small detached marks and a long low terminal join. The interior letters of liaison are not separable at enlarged view.
A large looped d-like beginning is visible, but the following small joins intersect a diagonal and the long cancellation. The o, n, and terminal c cannot all be independently secured.

At the end of the marginal sentence, low horizontal joins and short upright remnants overlap perpendicular main-text strokes. The proposed espace is not securely segmented; the box encloses the uncertain line ending and the continuation before the formula.

The final member has two distinct opening vertical bars, one baseline u with two stems joined by a bowl, and two distinct closing vertical bars. There is no sigma loop, i subscript, or pair of curved parentheses in this member.
A curved initial upright and two downward hooks survive below the black strike, while the latter letters coincide with black and red overdraw. The full sequence Supposons cannot be verified.
The canceled opening has an S-like curve, a low bowl, and short uprights along the strike. The i and the separate est and un groups are too covered to assert the complete four-part phrase.
Under the larger E, the earlier character has a left upright, a second central upright, and a connecting middle crossbar. Those surviving strokes support H; its center remains densely overwritten.

A descender, a tall crossed stroke, and a detached curved accent-like mark survive near the right of the canceled word. The body and ending are covered, so the full proposed comprises is not established.
The initial s is followed by a deep y descender, a short s join, and a crossed t. The following low ème joins and a raised accent mark support système, though the accent is compact.

An initial curved upright and two low clusters survive under the cancellation, with the following lambda stroke crossing below. The joins do not securely establish either the two words les valeurs or the repeated p structure of propres.
The character is covered by dense oblique and horizontal hatching. Upper and middle bars remain, but a putative lower bar cannot be separated from the cancellation, so E and F remain unresolved.

At the right of the deleted phrase, two short uprights and lower hooks remain along a heavy horizontal strike. The initial a, complete ppl sequence, and final abbreviation point are not independently clear.
The raised group has a curved opening parenthesis, one thick straight upright 1, and a curved closing parenthesis. The central stroke lacks the bent head and lower return needed for 2.

The final isolated f has a tall rising stroke, crossing arm and long lower hook, followed by blank paper rather than ini. The preceding proposed word rang is crossed by two dense horizontal strokes; its internal letters cannot all be distinguished.
Between the clear il and following se, a descending p-like stem and a terminal rising stroke survive. The cancellation absorbs the middle joins, so the complete proposed word peut remains unverified.

The inspected word has low rounded opening strokes, an extended overstruck middle, two rising strokes near the end and a hooked rightward return. The strikes cover the interior joins, so the ble-like ending does not establish the complete convenable sequence or exclude a masked final t; both supplied candidates remain uncertain.

A low opening curve, a central upright, one detached dot and a short final horizontal body survive in this word. The crossing line conceals the intervening letters and exact ending, so certain is retained as uncertain.

The word has an initial e-like loop, a separate small s-like remnant and a clear descending p. The following low letter bodies merge into the strike, preventing independent verification of the complete espace ending.

Immediately before the following dont is a tall narrow stroke with a low rightward return. The deletion crosses the short preceding and following joins, so three distinct letters t, e and l cannot be established.

The inserted word starts with a pointed capital A and crossbar, followed by a tall looped l, compact o, short r shoulder and final s return. The upper-line descender and two cancellation strokes cross it without removing that sequence.

In the inserted line after un, the surviving piece has a descending slant and an adjoining horizontal body. Multiple cancellation lines obscure its top and continuation; the remnant does not establish either the entire proposed tel or an isolated replacement letter.

The baseline u is followed above by a separate minus stroke and upright 1. At baseline the opening parenthesis curves into a small oval 0, and a separate curved closing parenthesis follows; both parentheses are present.

The opening has a tall l with a high adjoining apostrophe flick, followed by a dotted i. The compressed middle runs into a long descending g and a rightward terminal e hook, supporting the complete word.

The underlined word begins with a dotted i, then low n/v forms, a rounded a and r shoulder, a second dotted i and terminal e. Its dotted initial and lack of an opening co loop distinguish invarie from conserve.
A small closed lower loop with a tall ascender establishes the initial d beneath the insertion arrow. The neighboring short body is overstruck, and no independent i stem or dot can be isolated.

Immediately after E with its lower 1 is a separate right closing brace: its upper inward hook, central outward notch and lower inward return are visible. This is the whole literal brace candidate from the balanced source macro.

The canceled group contains two oblique arms meeting in a Λ apex, followed by a separate upright E with top, middle and bottom bars. Both baseline symbols are visible beneath the diagonal and horizontal strikes, excluding E or F alone.

Below the summation sign are a rounded 0, an angle with lower bar, a narrow p stem with right-hand loop, a second angle with lower dot-like bar, and a final low n. The photo edge crowds the p descender, but those five components remain distinguishable.
